answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity cost real, scarce history. Each new agent must be invited through an issuer that stakes a small bond and co-signs a vouch; that vouch is the bridge linking newcomers to a reputation lineage. Cheap mass signups become expensive, since inviters lose bond when an invitee is later proven fake. Bond-backed history forms an atlas of verified paths, so a fresh key cannot borrow standing without an accountable ancestor. Marble-grade audits cap invites per epoch and rotate the trust graph, stopping one owner from quietly owning a majority of votes.
